_comment: THE ONLY FILE YOU EDIT TO ADD OR REMOVE SOMETHING. Add a line, commit, done.

_status_meanings.held: you own it — moves are alerted and it appears in every digest
_status_meanings.watching: you do not own it yet — alerted the same way, but the LLM is told you are deciding, not holding
_status_meanings.muted: kept in the file for later, never fetched, never alerted

positions.note: small cap, expect noise — see move_pct
trades weekends; see the weekend note in triggers.py

_per_symbol_overrides: move_pct sets the single-day move that counts as urgent for ONE symbol. Omitted means the default in triggers.py.

macro._comment: FRED series. Free, needs FRED_API_KEY. Omit the key and these are skipped with a stated reason, not silently.
macro._move_thresholds: an absolute one-day change that counts as urgent

themes: US-Iran diplomacy, Strait of Hormuz, oil supply and Middle East conflict
US-China trade talks, tariffs, rare earths, AI export controls
Federal Reserve rate decisions, inflation prints and Fed official commentary
AI capital spending by large technology companies
US politics: elections, government funding, legislation affecting markets or taxes
anything a head of state, finance minister or central banker says about the economy
_feeds_comment: BROAD NEWS, NOT JUST YOUR TICKERS. A per-symbol feed can only ever mention a company already on your list, so it cannot warn you about a Fed decision, a Hormuz closure or an election result — the things that move holdings without naming them. Official sources are listed first on purpose: a central bank's own statement is the thing itself, where a news story about it is a report of it. Delete any that get noisy. Every fetch reports its own failure, so a dead feed is named in the letter.
_feed_limit: headlines taken per feed. Higher costs a little more to summarise.
